label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
**An open letter to everyone who’s been checking in**

To my friends, neighbours, the Little Acorns families, and everyone this reaches after it’s been forwarded: thank you for caring about me. My phone has been going nonstop since Saturday night, and I’m sorry I haven’t been able to answer everyone individually. I’m safe, Marmalade is safe, and I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch. I’m just very tired, so please don’t take it personally if I’m slow to reply to messages or comments.

On Saturday, 7 November, a fire started at around 11:40pm in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Obs. I live in flat 12, on the second floor. Everyone got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and sent home. The fire department says an electrical fault is a possibility, but the cause is still being investigated, so I don’t want to guess.

My flat has extensive smoke and water damage, and the lounge ceiling came down. The landlord has told us nobody will be able to go back in for at least six weeks. I woke when my neighbour, Uncle Faizel, went door to door on our floor in his vest and slippers, banging on every door. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade and got out. I didn’t take anything else. Marmalade hid under a car for two hours afterwards, which was terrifying, but she’s okay now. Furniture and belongings can be replaced. Marmalade can’t.

I don’t want to go through every detail of that night, but I do want to say how grateful I am for the people who helped us get out and for everyone who has checked in since. I’ve been crying at every message. One of the Little Acorns parents even left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday without waking anyone. That kindness means more than I can say.

Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy fundraiser to help me cover the deposit for a new place and get back on my feet. I feel awkward asking for help, but she told me to stop arguing and accept it, so I’m trying. The page is **backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**. The target is R25,000, and it had reached R11,400 this morning. If you’d like to contribute or share the link, thank you. Please use that link, and check that it’s Zinhle’s page before donating.

**A warning:** there’s another page called “Thandi Fire Relief” being circulated on an unfamiliar site, along with a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money to a Capitec account. That is **not my fundraiser**, and I have reported it. Please don’t send money to that page or account. If you’re unsure, ask me or someone who knows me before donating.

If you’re able to help in another way, what I need most right now is:

- Help with the deposit for a new place
- School shoes or work clothes in size 6 / size 34
- A working older laptop, if anyone has one they no longer need. My lesson planning was on the laptop that was lost in the fire.

What I **don’t** need is more general clothing; I already have plenty and will pass extra items on to residents from the other flats. I also don’t need food—my sister’s freezer is full. Please don’t feel you need to buy or bring anything. Sharing the fundraiser or simply sending a kind thought is already a lot.

To the Little Acorns families: I teach the Ladybirds, the Grade 00 class of four- and five-year-olds. The end-of-year concert on 27 November is still happening, so please don’t worry. The crowns and handprint banner I’d taken home to laminate were lost, including 22 crowns, but the Ladybirds will have crowns. We’ll sort it out.

I’ll be back at school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of the fire in front of the children; I’d like to keep their school day as ordinary and happy as possible.

Thank you for giving me time to catch my breath, and for being so generous and thoughtful. I’ll reply as I can, but it may take a while. I’m safe, Marmalade is safe, and I’m taking things one step at a time.

With love and thanks,  
**Thandi**
